title.narrative: Response to Integrated GBV case management, support in East and Horo Guduro Wollega zones Kiremu, Sasiga, Gida Ayana ,Jarte Jardaga, Amuru amp; Horo Buluk districts of Oromia Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed action provides integrated GBV case management, MHPSS and legal assistance, including capacity building on case management and MHPSS, in East Horo Guduru Wollega zones, Oromia Region, Kiremu, Sasiga, Gida Ayana, Jarte Jardega, Amuru Horo Buluk district. The action primarily focuses on 23617 (16,532 Female) population critically affected communities by prolonged conflict impact in the area. The conflict has manifested itself in huge damage the lives livelihood assets of the affected communities, The proposed action will alleviate the suffering of conflict -affected populations through anintegrated GBV case management, MHPSS legal assistance, including capacity building on case management and MHPSS. ltspangtAdhering to the IASC statement on the centrality of protection and policy on protection in humanitarian action, SOS and its sub implementing partners reaffirms that the protection of all affected and at risk individuals and communities must be at the heart of human decision-making. All humanitarians have the responsibility to protect affected or at risk individuals and communities before, during and after a crisis strikes. Inclusive participation to decision-making processes is fostered to support the development of self-protection capacities and assist people to claim their rights. .lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will conduct 1 protection risk and SGBV analysis and inform the implementation of the project facilitate referrals for 500 survivors to specialized services tailored to their specific needs, including medical care, psychosocial support, and legal aidtransfer multipurpose cash assistance directly to 1487 survivors of Sexual and Gender Based Violence (SGBV) and at-risk women and girls to empower them in meeting their immediate needs and supporting their recovery processfacilitate survival centered SGBV case management plans for 600 girls and boys, considering their diversity-age, gender, disabilities etc, to provide tailored support for reintegration,counseling, and other interventions based on their individual circumstancesprovide training for 160 SGBV survivors on empowerment, self-confidence etc and organze safe space for SGBV survivors to share their experiences.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt Conduct customized awareness training sessions for 160 community group representatives (including Anti-HTP committees, SHGs, child protection committees, and women and youth associations) on the available services for GBV survivors establish/strengthen 6 community-based referral pathwaysltbrgtfacilitate core GBV response service referral pathways to 400 vulnerable women and girlsorganize 16 quarterly referral network meetings for community coordination structures provide training for 48 health workers and project staff on MHPSS service standards 54 care providers working with GBV survivors will be trained to address trauma through supervisory counseling and 64 law enforcement actors will trained on case management and GBV survivors handling, and legal assistance 60 Community SGBV monitoring groups consists of divers groups representing local government,CBO, women, and youth association who will play a watchdog role in monitoring and reporting SGBV cases and build their capacity established16 community awareness-raising campaigns on GBV, PSEA, and SRHR conducted 400 IEC materials on GBV using the local language will be disseminated 16 women and girls’ safe spaces will be established or strengthend160 will organized on peer-to-peer education session on SGBV, child right, human right, gender equality etc and training will be provided on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) for 15 project team and support them to undergo an online line assessment test. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will be implemented over 12 months and require USD 1,000,000. to achieve its intended objectives of providing critical lifesaving protection services to affected communities. The Project will be implemented in consortium with two national and NGOs (SEED and We- Action) ltbrgtlt/pgt
